Alfred C. Finn.label: Alfred C. Finn
Alfred C. Finn.subtitle: 1883-1964 · Gulf Bldg, San Jacinto Monument & Downtown Towers
Alfred C. Finn.summary: Born in Bellville, Texas, Finn trained under Sanguinet & Staats before opening his Houston practice in 1913. Working closely with Jesse H. Jones, he shaped Houston's early-to-mid-20th-century skyline with the Gulf Building (1929), San Jacinto Monument (1939), Roy G. Cullen Building (1939) and Ezekiel W. Cullen Building (1950) at UH, and City National Bank (1947).

John F. Staub.label: John F. Staub
John F. Staub.subtitle: 1892-1981 · Bayou Bend, River Oaks, Broadacres & Rice/UH
John F. Staub.summary: MIT-trained architect who arrived in Houston in 1921 for Harrie T. Lindeberg and established his independent practice in 1923. Renowned for Bayou Bend (1928) and refined Georgian, Colonial Revival, and Regional houses in Shadyside, Broadacres, and River Oaks, as well as buildings for Rice University and the University of Houston.

Birdsall P. Briscoe.label: Birdsall P. Briscoe
Birdsall P. Briscoe.subtitle: 1876-1971 · Courtlandt Place, River Oaks & HABS Preservationist
Birdsall P. Briscoe.summary: Partnered with Maurice J. Sullivan (1912-1917) and collaborated frequently with John F. Staub across Courtlandt Place, Shadyside, Broadacres, and River Oaks. In the 1930s Briscoe served as South Texas district officer for the Historic American Buildings Survey (HABS).

William Ward Watkin.label: William Ward Watkin
William Ward Watkin.subtitle: 1886-1952 · Julia Ideson Bldg, MFAH & Founding Rice Arch. Chair
William Ward Watkin.summary: Sent to Houston at age 23 by Cram, Goodhue & Ferguson to supervise construction of Rice Institute's Lovett Hall (1910-1912), Watkin founded Rice's Department of Architecture and designed the Julia Ideson Building (1926), MFAH original neoclassical wing (1924), and Trinity Episcopal Church.

Joseph Finger.label: Joseph Finger
Joseph Finger.subtitle: 1887-1953 · City Hall, 1940 Airport Terminal & Art Deco Master
Joseph Finger.summary: Austrian-born architect who settled in Houston in 1908 and became the city's foremost exponent of Art Deco and PWA Moderne civic and commercial architecture, designing Houston City Hall (1939), the 1940 Houston Municipal Airport Terminal, the 1937 Jefferson Davis Hospital (with Alfred C. Finn, demolished), Temple Beth Israel (1925), and Texas State Hotel (1929).

Sanguinet & Staats.label: Sanguinet & Staats
Sanguinet & Staats.subtitle: Early Steel-Frame Downtown Skyscrapers & Courtlandt Place
Sanguinet & Staats.summary: Operating a major Houston office managed by Alfred C. Finn and R. D. Gottlieb, Sanguinet & Staats pioneered steel-frame commercial high-rises in Downtown Houston alongside grand residential mansions in Courtlandt Place and Montrose.

Olle J. Lorehn.label: Olle J. Lorehn
Olle J. Lorehn.subtitle: 1864-1939 · Binz Bldg, Fire Station No. 7 & Civic Landmarks
Olle J. Lorehn.summary: Swedish-born Houston architect and the second architect licensed in Texas; designed the six-story Binz Building (1895, demolished), Fire Station No. 7 (1899, now Houston Fire Museum), Sacred Heart Church (1912), and early civic and commercial landmarks.

Lamar Q. Cato.label: Lamar Q. Cato
Lamar Q. Cato.subtitle: 1888-1948 · UH Cullen Bldg, TSU Campus & HISD Schools
Lamar Q. Cato.summary: Former Houston City Architect who partnered with Joseph Finger (1920-1923) and designed major educational and civic landmarks including the Roy G. Cullen Building at the University of Houston (1939), initial 1946-1947 campus buildings for what became Texas Southern University, Houston ISD schools, and county courthouses.

Charles W. Oliver.label: Charles W. Oliver
Charles W. Oliver.subtitle: 1892-1960 · River Oaks, Montrose & Boulevard Oaks Residences
Charles W. Oliver.summary: Prolific residential architect whose brick Tudor Revival, English Cottage, and Colonial Revival homes define blocks of River Oaks, Montrose, and Boulevard Oaks.

Maurice J. Sullivan.label: Maurice J. Sullivan
Maurice J. Sullivan.subtitle: 1884-1961 · Houston City Architect, Catholic Churches & Schools
Maurice J. Sullivan.summary: Served as Houston City Architect (1912-1919), partnered with Birdsall P. Briscoe, and designed numerous Roman Catholic churches, schools, hospitals, and residences across Houston.

Eugene T. Heiner.label: Eugene T. Heiner
Eugene T. Heiner.subtitle: 1852-1901 · 1884 Cotton Exchange, American Brewing & Victorian Blocks
Eugene T. Heiner.summary: German-trained Victorian architect who designed cotton exchanges, breweries, courthouses, and brick commercial blocks across 1870s-1890s Houston and Texas.

George E. Dickey.label: George E. Dickey
George E. Dickey.subtitle: 1840-c.1906 · Gilded Age Romanesque & Victorian Main St Landmarks
George E. Dickey.summary: Leading late-19th-century Houston architect whose Romanesque Revival and Victorian brick landmarks defined 1880s-1900s Main Street, Market Square, and Quality Hill.

Stayton Nunn.label: Stayton Nunn
Stayton Nunn.subtitle: 1899-1960 · HISD Coordinating Architect, River Oaks & Civic Works
Stayton Nunn.summary: Coordinating architect for Houston ISD's postwar school building program, partner of Milton McGinty, and designer of refined residences across River Oaks, Montrose, and Broadacres.

Cameron D. Fairchild.label: Cameron D. Fairchild
Cameron D. Fairchild.subtitle: 1902-1985 · Texas Regionalist & Regency Homes in River Oaks
Cameron D. Fairchild.summary: Houston architect celebrated for sensitive Texas Regionalist, Colonial Revival, and Regency residences in River Oaks as well as refined commercial and institutional landmarks.

Hedrick & Gottlieb.label: Hedrick & Gottlieb
Hedrick & Gottlieb.subtitle: 1920s Skyscrapers, Niels Esperson Bldg & Medical Arts Towers
Hedrick & Gottlieb.summary: 1920s Skyscrapers, Niels Esperson Bldg & Medical Arts Towers. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Hedrick & Gottlieb across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Cram, Goodhue & Ferguson.label: Cram, Goodhue & Ferguson
Cram, Goodhue & Ferguson.subtitle: Rice Institute 1910 Campus Plan, Lovett Hall & Trinity Church
Cram, Goodhue & Ferguson.summary: Boston and New York firm led by Ralph Adams Cram that authored the 1910 General Plan for Rice Institute, Lovett Hall (1912), Mechanical Laboratory, and Trinity Episcopal Church in Midtown.

Nicholas J. Clayton.label: Nicholas J. Clayton
Nicholas J. Clayton.subtitle: 1840-1916 · High Victorian Gothic & Sacred Heart Co-Cathedral
Nicholas J. Clayton.summary: Texas's premier 19th-century Victorian architect, whose Houston works included Sacred Heart Co-Cathedral (1897, demolished), Annunciation Catholic Church additions, and Gilded Age institutional buildings.

James Ruskin Bailey.label: James Ruskin Bailey
James Ruskin Bailey.subtitle: 1889-1959 · Kirby Mansion 1928 Remodel, Sterne & Barringer-Norton Bldgs
James Ruskin Bailey.summary: Designed prominent Period Revival residences and commercial landmarks for Houston civic leaders, including the 1926-1928 Tudor Revival transformation of the 1894 John Henry Kirby Mansion at 2000 Smith Street (demolished November 2026).

Joseph W. Northrop Jr..label: Joseph W. Northrop Jr.
Joseph W. Northrop Jr..subtitle: 1886-1969 · Cram-Trained Residential & Church Architect
Joseph W. Northrop Jr..summary: 1886-1969 · Cram-Trained Residential & Church Architect. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Joseph W. Northrop Jr. across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

R. D. Steele.label: R. D. Steele
R. D. Steele.subtitle: 1855-1934 · First National Bank Bldg, Carnegie Library & Mansions
R. D. Steele.summary: 1855-1934 · First National Bank Bldg, Carnegie Library & Mansions. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to R. D. Steele across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

John S. Chase.label: John S. Chase
John S. Chase.subtitle: 1925-2012 · First Licensed Black Architect in TX, NOMA Co-Founder
John S. Chase.summary: In 1950 Chase became the first African American admitted to the University of Texas School of Architecture (earning his M.Arch. in 1952), and in 1954 became the first licensed African American architect in Texas. He co-founded the National Organization of Minority Architects (NOMA) and designed landmark Modernist churches, residences, and campus buildings at Texas Southern University and downtown Houston.

MacKie & Kamrath.label: MacKie & Kamrath
MacKie & Kamrath.subtitle: Est. 1937 · Wrightian Organic Modernism, Temple Emanu El & MDA
MacKie & Kamrath.summary: Deeply influenced by Frank Lloyd Wright's Usonian and Taliesin principles, MacKie & Kamrath brought bold geometric Organic Modernism to Houston through Temple Emanu El (1949), the M. D. Anderson Cancer Center, contemporary residences, and commercial buildings.

Philip Johnson & John Burgee.label: Philip Johnson & John Burgee
Philip Johnson & John Burgee.subtitle: 1906-2005 · Pennzoil Place, Menil/UST, Bank of America & Williams Tower
Philip Johnson & John Burgee.summary: Working extensively with Houston patrons Dominique and John de Menil and developer Gerald D. Hines, Johnson (and partner John Burgee on his 1975-1985 towers) made Houston a showcase of late-20th-century architecture through the University of St. Thomas Academic Mall (1957-1959), Pennzoil Place (1975-1976), Bank of America Center (1983), Williams Tower (1983), the Waterwall (1985), and Chapel of St. Basil (1997).

Caudill Rowlett Scott (CRS).label: Caudill Rowlett Scott (CRS)
Caudill Rowlett Scott (CRS).subtitle: Pioneering Modernist Educational, Civic & Jones Hall Architecture
Caudill Rowlett Scott (CRS).summary: Founded in 1946 by William Wayne Caudill and John Miles Rowlett, CRS revolutionized postwar school, university, and civic architecture and designed Jesse H. Jones Hall for the Performing Arts (1966) in Downtown Houston.

Kenneth Franzheim.label: Kenneth Franzheim
Kenneth Franzheim.subtitle: 1890-1959 · Bank of the Southwest, Foley's & Mid-Century Corporate Towers
Kenneth Franzheim.summary: New York and Houston architect who reshaped postwar Downtown Houston with Foley's Department Store (1947, demolished), Bank of the Southwest (1956), Texas National Bank (1955), and Humble Oil Building additions.

Wilson, Morris, Crain & Anderson.label: Wilson, Morris, Crain & Anderson
Wilson, Morris, Crain & Anderson.subtitle: 1965 Astrodome, Houston Post, One Shell Plaza & Museum Wings
Wilson, Morris, Crain & Anderson.summary: Co-architects (with Lloyd & Morgan) of the 1965 Astrodome and designers of major Houston Modernist corporate towers, museum wings, and civic libraries.

Harvin C. Moore & Hermon Lloyd.label: Harvin C. Moore & Hermon Lloyd
Harvin C. Moore & Hermon Lloyd.subtitle: Period Revival Residences, Astrodome Co-Architects & Civic Modernism
Harvin C. Moore & Hermon Lloyd.summary: Houston architectural partnership responsible for distinguished Period Revival homes in River Oaks and Montrose as well as major mid-century civic commissions including the 1965 Astrodome (as Lloyd & Morgan).

Golemon & Rolfe.label: Golemon & Rolfe
Golemon & Rolfe.subtitle: Mid-Century Modernist Schools, Churches, St. Joseph Hospital & IAH
Golemon & Rolfe.summary: Mid-Century Modernist Schools, Churches, St. Joseph Hospital & IAH. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Golemon & Rolfe across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

PGAL (Pierce Goodwin Alexander).subtitle: Houston Civic, Aviation, Museum & Campus Architecture (Est. 1946)
PGAL (Pierce Goodwin Alexander).summary: Houston Civic, Aviation, Museum & Campus Architecture (Est. 1946). Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to PGAL (Pierce Goodwin Alexander) across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

George Pierce & Abel B. Pierce.summary: Mid-Century Modernist Campus, Civic & Commercial Landmarks. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to George Pierce & Abel B. Pierce across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Cesar Pelli & Associates.summary: Four Leaf Towers, Herring Hall (Rice) & 1500 Louisiana. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Cesar Pelli & Associates across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

SOM (Skidmore, Owings & Merrill).summary: First City National Bank (1961), Wells Fargo Plaza & Tenneco Bldg. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to SOM (Skidmore, Owings & Merrill) across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Hopkins Architects.label: Hopkins Architects
Hopkins Architects.subtitle: Rice University Duncan Hall, Brockman Hall & Contemporary Campus Works
Hopkins Architects.summary: Rice University Duncan Hall, Brockman Hall & Contemporary Campus Works. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Hopkins Architects across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Lake|Flato Architects.subtitle: Texas Regional Modernism, Rice University & Hermann Park Pavilions
Lake|Flato Architects.summary: Texas Regional Modernism, Rice University & Hermann Park Pavilions. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Lake|Flato Architects across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Machado and Silvetti.summary: Rice University Campus Halls & Contemporary Institutional Design. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Machado and Silvetti across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Ulrich Franzen.summary: 1968 Alley Theatre Brutalist Landmark. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Ulrich Franzen across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Hamilton Brown.subtitle: Mid-Century Modern Churches, Schools & Residential Architecture
Hamilton Brown.summary: Mid-Century Modern Churches, Schools & Residential Architecture. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Hamilton Brown across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Russell Brown Co..label: Russell Brown Co.
Russell Brown Co..subtitle: Early-20th-Century Pattern-Book Residences in Montrose & Courtlandt Pl
Russell Brown Co..summary: Prominent Houston residential design-build firm known for published pattern-book plans (such as Model Residences No. 203, 204, and 211) and finely crafted Craftsman, Prairie, and Colonial Revival homes across Montrose, Avondale, Courtlandt Place, and Woodland Heights.

Salisbury & McHale.label: Salisbury & McHale
Salisbury & McHale.subtitle: 1920s English Cottage, Tudor & Colonial Revival Builder-Architects
Salisbury & McHale.summary: 1920s English Cottage, Tudor & Colonial Revival Builder-Architects. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Salisbury & McHale across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

American Construction Company.label: American Construction Company
American Construction Company.subtitle: Gulf Bldg, Niels Esperson Bldg & Major Downtown High-Rise Builder
American Construction Company.summary: Gulf Bldg, Niels Esperson Bldg & Major Downtown High-Rise Builder. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to American Construction Company across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

W. S. Bellows Construction Corp..label: W. S. Bellows Construction Corp.
W. S. Bellows Construction Corp..subtitle: San Jacinto Monument, City Hall & Major Houston Skyscraper Builder
W. S. Bellows Construction Corp..summary: San Jacinto Monument, City Hall & Major Houston Skyscraper Builder. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to W. S. Bellows Construction Corp. across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

W. L. Webber & Associates.label: W. L. Webber & Associates
W. L. Webber & Associates.subtitle: Early-20th-Century Streetcar Suburb Residential Builder
W. L. Webber & Associates.summary: Early-20th-Century Streetcar Suburb Residential Builder. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to W. L. Webber & Associates across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Hart Oil & Well Co. (Builder).label: Hart Oil & Well Co. (Builder)
Hart Oil & Well Co. (Builder).subtitle: Historic Residential & Commercial Builder in Houston
Hart Oil & Well Co. (Builder).summary: Historic Residential & Commercial Builder in Houston. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Hart Oil & Well Co. (Builder) across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Independence Heights Builders.label: Independence Heights Builders
Independence Heights Builders.subtitle: Early-20th-Century Black Contractors in Texas's First Black Municipality
Independence Heights Builders.summary: Early-20th-Century Black Contractors in Texas's First Black Municipality. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Independence Heights Builders across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Jeff Bland Lumber Co. (Freedmen's Town).label: Jeff Bland Lumber Co. (Freedmen's Town)
Jeff Bland Lumber Co. (Freedmen's Town).subtitle: Early-1900s Freedmen's Town Folk Victorian & Shotgun Home Builder
Jeff Bland Lumber Co. (Freedmen's Town).summary: Early-1900s Freedmen's Town Folk Victorian & Shotgun Home Builder. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Jeff Bland Lumber Co. (Freedmen's Town) across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Bungalow (All Variants).label: Bungalow (All Variants)
Bungalow (All Variants).subtitle: 1900-1938 · Norhill, Heights, Woodland Heights & Eastwood Bungalows
Bungalow (All Variants).summary: Encompassing gable-front, hipped, pedimented, English, and duplex bungalows across Norhill, Houston Heights, Woodland Heights, Eastwood, and Montrose, the early-20th-century bungalow forms the backbone of Houston's streetcar-suburb housing stock.

Craftsman Style.label: Craftsman Style
Craftsman Style.subtitle: 1905-1935 · Exposed Rafter Tails, Tapered Columns & Deep Eaves
Craftsman Style.summary: Defined by low-pitched gabled roofs, deep overhanging eaves with exposed rafter tails, tapered porch columns on brick piers, and double-hung multi-over-one wood windows across Norhill, Houston Heights, Woodland Heights, and Eastwood.

Gable-Front & Pyramid Cottages.label: Gable-Front & Pyramid Cottages
Gable-Front & Pyramid Cottages.subtitle: 1885-1930 · Hipped-Roof & Gable-Front Streetcar Suburb Cottages
Gable-Front & Pyramid Cottages.summary: 1885-1930 · Hipped-Roof & Gable-Front Streetcar Suburb Cottages. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Gable-Front & Pyramid Cottages across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

American Foursquare.label: American Foursquare
American Foursquare.subtitle: 1900-1925 · Two-Story Cubic Massing, Hipped Dormer & Full Porch
American Foursquare.summary: Two-story boxy residences with hipped roofs, central dormers, four-room-per-floor plans, and full-width front porches across Houston Heights, Woodland Heights, Montrose, and Westmoreland.

Prairie School.label: Prairie School
Prairie School.subtitle: 1905-1925 · Low Hipped Roofs, Horizontal Banding & Broad Eaves
Prairie School.summary: Characterized by low-pitched hipped roofs with wide boxed eaves, horizontal stucco or brick banding, massive square porch piers, and ribbon windows across Courtlandt Place, Montrose, Avondale, and Woodland Heights.

Queen Anne Victorian.label: Queen Anne Victorian
Queen Anne Victorian.subtitle: 1880-1910 · Turrets, Wraparound Porches & Shingle Gables
Queen Anne Victorian.summary: Distinguished by asymmetrical massing, wraparound spindlework porches, corner turrets, imbricated wood shingles, and steeply pitched hipped-and-gabled roofs, best preserved in Old Sixth Ward and Houston Heights.

Folk Victorian.label: Folk Victorian
Folk Victorian.subtitle: 1875-1910 · Turned Spindlework Trim on Simple Gable Forms
Folk Victorian.summary: Defined by jigsaw-cut brackets, turned porch spindles, and decorative friezes applied to symmetrical L-plan, gable-front, or pyramidal cottages across Old Sixth Ward, Freedmen's Town, High First Ward, and Houston Heights.

Gothic Revival.label: Gothic Revival
Gothic Revival.subtitle: 1865-1940 · Pointed-Arch Lancet Windows, Buttresses & Spires
Gothic Revival.summary: Pointed-arch lancet windows, buttressed brick or limestone walls, and crenellated or spired bell towers found on historic sanctuaries such as Antioch Missionary Baptist Church (1875) and early downtown churches.

Italianate.label: Italianate
Italianate.subtitle: 1860-1895 · Bracketed Cornices, Tall Hooded Windows & Cupolas
Italianate.summary: 1860-1895 · Bracketed Cornices, Tall Hooded Windows & Cupolas. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Italianate across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Shotgun & Folk Vernacular.summary: 1875-1925 · Single-Room-Wide Linear Homes Across Historic Wards. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Shotgun & Folk Vernacular across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Second Empire.label: Second Empire
Second Empire.subtitle: 1870-1895 · Mansard Roofs with Dormers & Cast-Iron Cresting
Second Empire.summary: 1870-1895 · Mansard Roofs with Dormers & Cast-Iron Cresting. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Second Empire across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Colonial Revival.label: Colonial Revival
Colonial Revival.subtitle: 1895-1955 · Symmetrical Facades, Pedimented Entries & Multi-Pane Sash
Colonial Revival.summary: Drawing on Georgian, Federal, and Southern classical precedents with symmetrical facades, pedimented entries, and multi-pane sash windows, Colonial Revival spans Houston's streetcar suburbs and garden estates.

English Cottage & Picturesque.label: English Cottage & Picturesque
English Cottage & Picturesque.subtitle: 1920-1940 · Asymmetrical Brick Gables, Arched Doors & Storybook Massing
English Cottage & Picturesque.summary: 1920-1940 · Asymmetrical Brick Gables, Arched Doors & Storybook Massing. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to English Cottage & Picturesque across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Tudor Revival Style.label: Tudor Revival Style
Tudor Revival Style.subtitle: 1915-1940 · Steep Cross Gables, Half-Timbering & Leaded Casements
Tudor Revival Style.summary: Marked by steeply pitched cross gables, patterned brick and half-timbering, tall chimney pots, and leaded casement windows, Tudor Revival became a signature residential style across River Oaks, Boulevard Oaks, Montrose, and Woodland Heights.

Georgian Revival.label: Georgian Revival
Georgian Revival.subtitle: 1910-1945 · Formal Red-Brick Symmetry, Dentil Cornices & Palladian Motifs
Georgian Revival.summary: 1910-1945 · Formal Red-Brick Symmetry, Dentil Cornices & Palladian Motifs. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Georgian Revival across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

French Eclectic & Normandy.subtitle: 1920-1945 · Steep Hipped Roofs, Round Stair Towers & Casement Windows
French Eclectic & Normandy.summary: 1920-1945 · Steep Hipped Roofs, Round Stair Towers & Casement Windows. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to French Eclectic & Normandy across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Beaux-Arts Classicism.label: Beaux-Arts Classicism
Beaux-Arts Classicism.subtitle: 1895-1930 · Paired Columns, Sculptural Cartouches & Civic Grandeur
Beaux-Arts Classicism.summary: 1895-1930 · Paired Columns, Sculptural Cartouches & Civic Grandeur. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Beaux-Arts Classicism across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Neoclassical & Classical Revival.label: Neoclassical & Classical Revival
Neoclassical & Classical Revival.subtitle: 1895-1940 · Monumental Colonnades, Porticos & Limestone Facades
Neoclassical & Classical Revival.summary: 1895-1940 · Monumental Colonnades, Porticos & Limestone Facades. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Neoclassical & Classical Revival across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Mission Revival.subtitle: 1905-1935 · Shaped Espadana Parapets, Clay Tile & Stucco Arcades

Traditional & Mid-Century Ranch.label: Traditional & Mid-Century Ranch
Traditional & Mid-Century Ranch.subtitle: 1945-1975 · Single-Story Postwar Suburban & Tudor/Modern Ranch Homes
Traditional & Mid-Century Ranch.summary: Single-story, ground-hugging postwar residences with low hipped or cross-gabled roofs, broad picture windows, brick wainscot or Roman brick walls, and integrated carports or garages across Glenbrook Valley, Idylwood, Oak Forest, and Meyerland.

Postmodern & Contemporary.subtitle: 1975-Present · Sculptural Towers, Contextual Forms & Modern Campus Works
Postmodern & Contemporary.summary: 1975-Present · Sculptural Towers, Contextual Forms & Modern Campus Works. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Postmodern & Contemporary across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.

Mid-Century Modern.label: Mid-Century Modern
Mid-Century Modern.subtitle: 1946-1972 · Low Horizontal Lines, Roman Brick & Floor-to-Ceiling Glass
Mid-Century Modern.summary: Emphasizing horizontal rooflines, Roman brick, floor-to-ceiling glass walls, carports, and indoor-outdoor courtyards across Glenbrook Valley, Memorial, Meyerland, and Houston's university campuses.

Art Deco Style.label: Art Deco Style
Art Deco Style.subtitle: 1925-1942 · Stepped Setbacks, Zigzag Terra-Cotta & Vertical Piers
Art Deco Style.summary: Characterized by stepped vertical piers, cast-stone or terra-cotta botanical and zigzag relief panels, limestone spandrels, and monumental setbacks, Art Deco flourished in Houston during the late-1920s oil boom and 1930s PWA civic building program.

Streamline & PWA Moderne.label: Streamline & PWA Moderne
Streamline & PWA Moderne.subtitle: 1933-1948 · Curved Corners, Glass Block, Speed Lines & Civic Limestone
Streamline & PWA Moderne.summary: Marked by aerodynamic curved corners, glass-block bands, horizontal speed lines, and stripped classical limestone facades across 1930s-1940s civic buildings, theaters, clinics, and commercial storefronts.

Brutalist & Late Modern.subtitle: 1965-1985 · Board-Formed Concrete, Sculptural Massing & Bold Geometry
Brutalist & Late Modern.summary: 1965-1985 · Board-Formed Concrete, Sculptural Massing & Bold Geometry. Chronological portfolio of extant and demolished structures attributed to Brutalist & Late Modern across Harris County archival, landmark, and curated survey records.
